Farmer fined £2,000 for illegal tree felling

21 March 2024

A farmer has been fined for illegally felling trees on his land in Powys.

John Kerwen Davies, 58, of Llwyn Farm, Llandrindod Wells, appeared at Llanelli Magistrates' Court on 21 March 2024 after admitting to felling trees without a felling licence.

The court heard that Davies had felled approximately 2 hectares of mature woodland on his farm between January and March 2023 without first obtaining the required licence from Natural Resources Wales.

NRW officers discovered the illegal felling during a routine inspection in April 2023. When questioned, Davies admitted he had not applied for a felling licence because he "didn't think he needed one for trees on his own land."

District Judge Sarah Williams said: "The requirement to obtain a felling licence exists to protect our woodland heritage. Ignorance of the law is no excuse."

Davies was fined £2,000 and ordered to pay £5,000 in prosecution costs, plus an £800 victim surcharge. He was also ordered to replant the felled area within two years.

Speaking after the hearing, NRW's Head of Operations for Mid Wales said: "This case demonstrates our commitment to protecting Wales's woodlands. Anyone considering felling trees should first check whether they need a licence."

The offence was committed contrary to Section 17 of the Forestry Act 1967.
